To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition to electric vehicles is a discontinuous technological change that leads to the simultaneous emergence of widely differing business model innovations and that the choice of a business model is a function of the technological competence, of the competitive advantage, of the value architecture, of the customer value proposition, of the profit model, and of the degree of change of the environment.

the decisions to innovate business model components in times of long-term discontinuous technological change are mainly influenced by the technological competence of the company, its strategic position and the technological competence of its competitors.

business models of incumbent companies in the transition from one technology to another can be classified into three groups, namely technology embracing, technology balancing, and technology postponing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how business models can be adapted to long term discontinuous technology changes.
the question of how companies in the automotive industry can successfully adapt their business models to the long term discontinuous change to electric mobility.

the question of how business model innovations can be described and analysed in the context of long term discontinous technological change, in particular the transition from the internal combustion engine to electric mobility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the competence based view is a useful framework for explaining the adaptation of business model innovations in times long term discontinuous technology change.

in the transition to the electric mobility, companies can choose from different paths of business model innovations and that these paths differ in terms of resource allocation, competitive advantage, value architecture, value proposition and profit models.
the competence based view is a suitable approach for investigating the adaptation of business model components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study show that the transition to the electric mobility is accompanied by a variety of innovations in business models.

business models can be adapted to the transition to electric vehicles through the innovation of their components, particularly through changes in the value architecture and customer value proposition, and that these adaptations can be achieved by means of a wide range of decisions.

the results of our empirical studies show that business model innovation decisions are not only driven by technological changes. In particular, they are driven by the companies' strategic orientation, their competitive position and their technological competence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decisions on business model components are not only influenced by the current situation of the company and its environment but are also strongly determined by the company’s strategic orientation.
business model innovations are not only driven by technological change, but also by changes in the market, especially the emergence of new customer segments.
the transition to electric vehicles is not a linear process, but rather a complex process that is characterized by a variety of business model innovations.
